title: Charitable schemes and school enrolment deposits
subject: This guide addresses how charities can raise funds by issuing debentures or interests in managed investment schemes, and provides relief from certain fundraising, managed investment, debenture, and licensing provisions of the Corporations Act. It also covers an exemption for schools accepting enrolment deposits from the fundraising provisions of the Corporations Act.
background: The guide is issued under the Corporations Act 2001 (Cth) and is intended for charities and schools seeking to raise funds. It explains ASIC's policy on granting relief from specific regulatory requirements to facilitate charitable fundraising while maintaining investor protection.
ruling: ASIC provides conditional relief to charitable investment fundraisers from the fundraising, managed investment, debenture, and licensing provisions of the Corporations Act, subject to compliance with ASIC Corporations (Charitable Investment Fundraising) Instrument 2016/813. For schools, ASIC grants an exemption from the fundraising provisions for enrolment deposits under ASIC Corporations (School Enrolment Deposits) Instrument 2016/812. The relief is designed to reduce regulatory burden while ensuring adequate disclosure and protection for investors. ASIC expects charities to operate with transparency and to adhere to the conditions set out in the relevant instruments. The guide also clarifies the definition of associates and the obligations of sponsors in the charitable investment fundraising context.
legislation_referenced: Australian Securities and Investments Commission Act 2001 (Cth)
